hero.title: Certifications & <accent>training</accent>
hero.lead: What's earned, what's in progress, what's targeted. No invented dates, no result presented as earned before it is.

certs.title: What's verifiable today
certs.lead: Two certifications structure the build-up of cloud and network skills.

az900.name: AZ-900, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
az900.description: The basics of Azure cloud: concepts, services, security, compliance and pricing.
az900.why: The AZ-900 lays the cloud fundamentals. It's my starting point: it opens the way to AZ-104 (Azure administration). A deliberate entry point, not a stack of certifications.

ccna.name: CCNA, Cisco
ccna.description: Reference network certification: switching, routing, basic infrastructure security.
ccna.why: Digging into cloud made one thing clear: you don't really master the cloud without mastering networks. So I branched into the CCNA, before coming back to AZ-104. Networks first, cloud after.

autoformation.label: Self-study
autoformation.text: TryHackMe: regular practice in defense (blue team) and networking, alongside the official certifications.

formation.title: A retraining that is built, not improvised
formation.lead: An ongoing higher-education degree, complemented by an intensive bootcamp and two development internships.

prior.heading: Before the retraining
prior.text: Telecom technician, Belgian Defence (2013-2017). Security officer, European Commission (2022-2023). Field experience and operational discipline, reinvested in cyber.
